paper_title: Constraints on axionlike dark matter with masses down to $10^{-23}$ eV/c$^2$
coupling_convention: dimensionless g_ae, converted from the paper's F_a/C_e > 2e15 eV bound via g_ae = C_e * m_e / F_a with m_e = 5.11e5 eV
notes: Terrano et al. (arXiv:1902.04246), Eot-Wash rotating torsion pendulum with ~1e23 polarized electrons, 6.7-year dataset, searching for axionlike dark-matter wind coupling to electron spin. Paper quotes a 95% CL limit F_a/C_e > 2e15 eV over much of the mass range 1e-23 to 1e-18 eV/c^2, which I converted to g_ae = m_e/(F_a/C_e) ~ 2.6e-10 and encoded as a flat two-point bound. Actual limit (Fig. 5) varies with mass: degraded near the sidereal frequency (m_a ~ 47 zeV = 4.7e-20 eV) and at the highest masses due to finite measurement-duration attenuation; detailed curve is in supplemental material, not extractable from text.
